hic

Notes

  1. 1hic: short i (Lewis & Short hīc, haec, hōc, marking the heavy syllable as a long vowel). De Vaan 284, s.v. hic: the nominative is *hi-ke, so the vowel is short and the syllable heavy (hicc, p. 102, s.v. -ce); the adverb hīc, here, is the old locative *hoi-ke.
  2. 2hic: short i (Lewis & Short hīc, haec, hōc, marking the heavy syllable as a long vowel). De Vaan 284, s.v. hic: the nominative is *hi-ke, so the vowel is short and the syllable heavy (hicc, p. 102, s.v. -ce); the adverb hīc, here, is the old locative *hoi-ke. Likewise the neuter hoc (hocc), against the ablative hōc.
  3. 3hic: short i (Lewis & Short hīc, haec, hōc, marking the heavy syllable as a long vowel). De Vaan 284, s.v. hic: the nominative is *hi-ke, so the vowel is short and the syllable heavy (hicc, p. 102, s.v. -ce); the adverb hīc, here, is the old locative *hoi-ke. As in the record for “current”.
